Topic: The Geometric Essence of Cross Products and Linear Transformations

Target audience: Undergraduate students in STEM

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: The Determinant and Area

Lecture lines:
Determinants measure the signed area of a parallelogram.
Linear transformations scale the area of the unit square.
This scaling factor reveals the transformation's underlying nature.

Planned animations:
Create a 2D grid morphing to visualize area change. Color: #FFFFFF.
Label 'Determinant' as the scaling factor of area. Color: #FFD700.
Display a transformation matrix M changing the grid. Color: #00FF00.

Section: section_2 — Defining the Cross Product in 3D

Lecture lines:
Cross products create vectors perpendicular to a plane.
The magnitude equals the area of the spanned parallelogram.
Visualize it as a flagpole rising from the floor.

Planned animations:
Render three vectors in 3D space: u, v, w. Color: #FF4500.
Animate the construction of the parallelepiped. Color: #1E90FF.
Flash the resulting vector n perpendicular to surface. Color: #FFFF00.
Label the cross product u x v clearly. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show the magnitude formula ||u|| ||v|| sin(theta). Color: #FF69B4.

Section: section_3 — Geometric Intuition: Orientation and Chirality

Lecture lines:
Orientation depends on the handedness of basis vectors.
Positive results follow a counter-clockwise path.
Negative results indicate a clockwise orientation.

Planned animations:
Animate the Right-Hand Rule with a hand icon. Color: #FFFFFF.
Rotate the vectors to show orientation preservation. Color: #00FFFF.
Highlight left-handed vs right-handed basis flip. Color: #FF0000.

Section: section_4 — Linear Transformations and the 'Area-to-Volume' Bridge

Lecture lines:
3D volumes are defined by three vectors.
The scalar triple product computes this volume.
It connects base area to final height.

Planned animations:
Show a unit cube transforming into a volume. Color: #87CEEB.
Draw a 3x3 determinant matrix mapping. Color: #32CD32.
Visualize the scaling factor as volume change. Color: #FFD700.
Connect the cross product to volume formulas. Color: #FF4500.
Label the transformation T as volume scalar. Color: #FFFFFF.

Section: section_5 — Application: Normal Vectors and Surfaces

Lecture lines:
Cross products help define surface normal vectors.
Normals are essential for calculating light reflections.
This enables realistic rendering of 3D models.

Planned animations:
Animate a plane surface with normal vector. Color: #FFFFFF.
Show vector lighting calculation using dot product. Color: #00FF00.
Flash normal vector adjustment with surface rotation. Color: #FFD700.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = [
            "Determinants measure the signed area of a parallelogram.",
            "Linear transformations scale the area of the unit square.",

        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: The Determinant and Area", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a 2D grid morphing to visualize area change.

        self.place_in_area(grid, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.place_at_grid(det_label, 'B4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(det_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.move_to(center)

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
